  • Spring Redis cache outage: choose failure behavior per operation
  • Spring STOMP broker relay: credentials and broker availability are separate from user identity
  • Spring WebSocket reconnect: recover state after an unobserved gap
  • Spring HTTP service groups: configure one host policy for several interfaces
  • Spring WebClient exchangeToMono: decode the response inside its callback
  • Reactive HTTP service client: the proxy returns a publisher, not a completed call

Document data, search and method security

  • Spring Data MongoDB tenant uniqueness: enforce it in an index
  • Spring Data MongoDB transaction: keep every write in one client session
  • Spring Data MongoDB bulk writes: fewer round trips, different lifecycle behavior
  • Spring Data MongoDB change stream: resume token and idempotent projection
  • Spring Data Elasticsearch write versus search: refresh is the visibility boundary
  • Spring Data Elasticsearch sequence conflict: do not overwrite a newer projection
  • Spring Data Elasticsearch mapping rollout: build a new index, then move the read alias
  • Spring method security: authorization advice runs through the bean proxy
  • Spring @PostAuthorize: denial happens after the method has run

Cassandra, Neo4j, Kubernetes and SAML

  • Spring Data Cassandra partition keys: model the read before the row
  • Spring Data Cassandra TTL: expiry is a storage and query cost
  • Spring Data Cassandra paging state: continue the same bounded query
  • Spring Data Neo4j relationships: save only the graph you own
  • Spring Data Neo4j transaction: keep the command inside one managed unit
  • Spring Data Neo4j version conflicts: reject a stale graph update
  • Spring Cloud Kubernetes config import: make source precedence explicit
  • Spring Cloud Kubernetes reload: decide which changes need a restart
  • Spring Cloud Kubernetes discovery: choose API lookup or Service DNS
  • Spring Security SAML relying party: align registration, ACS and metadata
  • Spring Security SAML validation: signatures, audience and clock window
  • Spring Security SAML attributes: map identity to local authority

Conditional writes, graph queries, cluster access and SAML sessions

  • Spring Data Cassandra conditional insert: reserve one key once
  • Spring Data Cassandra consistency: budget availability and staleness per operation
  • Spring Data Cassandra @Version: a conflict is not a merge
  • Spring Data Neo4j custom query: return one coherent root record
  • Spring Data Neo4j tenant lookup: constrain before traversing
  • Spring Data Neo4j relationship properties: preserve edge identity
  • Spring Cloud Kubernetes permissions: scope the service account to its reads
  • Spring Boot Kubernetes probes: separate startup, readiness and liveness
  • Spring Cloud Kubernetes watcher scope: filter before broadcasting refresh
  • Spring Security SAML logout: local session versus single logout
  • Spring SAML session revocation: closing the browser is not deprovisioning
  • Spring SAML certificate rollover: overlap trust without accepting unknown keys

Store and platform practice

  • Spring Cassandra write and query contracts quiz
  • Spring Neo4j graph mapping and query contracts quiz
  • Spring Kubernetes configuration and probe quiz
  • Spring SAML trust and session quiz

Web Development connection

Spring Boot Web Service Boundaries; Project: Spring Boot Permit Service Boundaries; Web Development: Spring Boot service contracts.

JPA query and transaction contracts

  • Spring Data JPA entity graph for a bounded to-one read
  • Spring Data JPA Specifications with a mandatory tenant predicate
  • Spring Data JPA Page versus Slice: pay for totals only when needed
  • Spring Data JPA count query for a joined Page
  • Spring Data JPA saveAndFlush is a SQL boundary, not a commit
  • Spring read-only transaction: performance hint, not a write guard
  • Spring Data JPA auditing: record the actor at the write boundary
  • Spring Boot Open EntityManager in View: close the response-time query gap

Spring testing boundaries

  • Spring Data JPA test: flush and clear before trusting a read
  • Spring Data JPA test against the deployment database dialect
  • Spring Boot HTTP test: client rollback does not own server writes
  • Spring MockMvc security test: run the application filter chain
  • Spring TestContext cache: keep equivalent tests on one context shape
  • Spring @MockitoBean override: a mock can remove advice from the tested bean
  • Spring transactional event test: cross an actual commit boundary
  • Spring scheduled worker test: inject a clock and call the work once

Container and security contracts

  • Spring BeanFactoryPostProcessor: inspect definitions before instances exist
  • Spring BeanPostProcessor: instance callbacks and the early-bean trap
  • Spring FactoryBean: expose the product type without constructing it
  • Spring SmartLifecycle phases: drain work before destroying dependencies
  • Spring Resource Server JWT key rotation: overlap keys across token lifetime
  • Spring password hash upgrade after a verified login
  • Spring SecurityContext handoff to a bounded async executor
  • Spring Security CORS preflight: evaluate origin before authentication

Management and cache contracts

  • Spring Actuator management port: separate listener, explicit access rule
  • Spring Prometheus scrape endpoint: registry, exposure and label contract
  • Spring health details: status for probes, diagnostics for operators
  • Spring cache after commit: keep rolled-back writes out of readers
  • Spring null-result caching: decide whether a miss should survive
  • Spring Redis cache serialization: roll payload formats without mixed readers
  • Spring tracing and logs: preserve request identity across outbound calls
  • Spring Actuator loggers endpoint: temporary diagnosis with guarded write access

Web runtime contracts

  • Spring MVC async executor: bound Callable work before requests pile up
  • Spring MVC streaming response: stop work when the client disconnects
  • Spring WebFlux codec memory budget: distinguish aggregation from streaming
  • Spring WebClient status-specific decoding: consume one branch and close the rest

Conditional auto-configuration contracts

  • Spring Boot ConditionalOnMissingBean: a default that yields to application code
  • Spring Boot ConditionalOnProperty: make optional infrastructure opt in

Virtual-thread admission

  • Spring Boot virtual threads: cheaper waiting still needs admission control

JPA identity and batching

Data and transactions now includes assigned-ID state, insert batching and collection fetch paging.

Security chain and token boundaries

Spring Security now includes multiple filter chains, JWT authority mapping and SPA CSRF token refresh.

Spring test isolation

Testing now covers MVC slices, SQL fixture transaction modes and preemptive timeout rollback risk.

Batch execution boundaries

Production now includes step-scoped readers, partition ownership and flow restart status.

Startup diagnostics and packaging boundaries

  • Spring Boot FailureAnalyzer: turn one startup exception into an actionable failure
  • Spring Boot condition report: locate the missing auto-configuration decision
  • Spring Boot configuration-property scanning: keep the package boundary explicit
  • Spring Boot layered jar: keep dependency changes out of the application layer
  • Spring Boot buildpack image: separate build settings from deployed secrets
  • Spring Boot executable jar: load resources through the classpath, not a file path
  • Spring Boot process exit codes: make job failure visible to the scheduler
  • Spring Boot DevTools restart: reproduce classloader failures without it
  • Spring Boot context initializer: make pre-refresh customization narrow

  • Spring JPA entity lifecycle: managed changes and detached objects
  • Spring JPA fetch plans: measure N+1 queries before changing mappings
  • Spring JPA optimistic locking: reject a stale stock update
  • Spring transaction propagation: joined rollback and independent commit
  • Spring Data JPA repositories: derive a query from mapped properties
  • Spring Data JPA projections: return selected fields without a full entity
  • Spring Data keyset pagination: continue after the last stable identifier
  • Spring transaction rollback: checked failures commit unless a rule says otherwise
  • Spring transactional outbox: commit a receipt and event row together
  • Spring outbox claims: move pending work once per database state
  • Spring nested transactions: roll back one step to a JDBC savepoint
  • Spring NESTED versus REQUIRES_NEW: savepoint or independent commit
  • Spring outbox claims: allow recovery after a worker lease expires
  • Outbox acknowledgements: require the current lease token
  • Spring consumer deduplication: commit the event ID with the mutation
  • Spring tenant command transaction: keep state, event and replay record together
  • Spring JDBC versioned tenant update: inspect the affected row count
  • Spring receipt outbox command: record intent without claiming delivery
  • Spring outbox relay: claim, deliver, and acknowledge one event
  • Spring outbox claims: lease expiry and token-fenced acknowledgement
  • Spring consumer idempotency: reserve an event ID with the stock mutation
  • Spring outbox transaction boundaries: where atomicity ends
  • Spring scheduled relay: recover when the consumer commits before acknowledgement
  • Spring outbox claim race: one conditional UPDATE wins
  • Spring outbox lease renewal: extend only the current owner
  • Spring database rollout: add a nullable column before changing every writer
  • Spring database backfill: assign historical rows before enforcing ownership
  • Spring database contract phase: reject old writers only after backfill
  • Spring Boot migrations: what a versioned runner must add to the SQL test
  • Flyway SQL migrations: record ordered schema changes against a real database
  • Flyway expand and contract: show exactly when an old writer breaks
  • Flyway validation: detect a changed applied migration before another write
  • Spring Boot Flyway startup: apply versioned SQL before querying a receipt
  • Spring Boot migration target: test an old writer before closing the schema
  • Spring Boot migration history failure: stop context startup on a mismatch

Boot Foundations, Spring Core, Web APIs, Security, Testing, Production, Exercises, Quizzes, Projects.

Database concurrency limits

  • Spring transaction isolation: state the anomaly you need to prevent

New checked lessons

  • Spring NamedParameterJdbcTemplate: expand an ID list without dropping tenant scope
  • Spring SimpleJdbcInsert: read the generated key after one insert

Kafka and database ownership

  • Spring Kafka duplicate delivery: let a unique event ID decide the second debit
  • Spring outbox to Kafka: name the crash window between send and relay acknowledgement

GraphQL data and mutation limits

  • Spring GraphQL list bounds: reject large arguments before reading rows
  • Spring GraphQL mutation versions: reject a stale stock reservation

R2DBC subscription and transaction contracts

  • Spring R2DBC subscription boundary: constructing SQL does not execute it
  • Spring R2DBC named binds: keep a receipt identifier out of SQL syntax
  • Spring R2DBC reactive transaction: roll back the event marker with a rejected debit
  • Spring R2DBC conditional update: test tenant, version and stock floor in one statement

Spring AI boundary lessons

  • Spring AI retrieval: apply the tenant filter before prompt assembly
  • Spring AI conversation memory: partition by verified tenant and caller

Batch restart and recovery

  • Spring Batch writers: use a stable source key when a chunk is replayed

Batch recovery and rejected-row review

  • Spring Batch restart input: pin the manifest before resuming a cursor
  • Spring Batch SkipListener: persist a rejection key with the skipped row

Batch metadata and hard-stop recovery

  • Spring Batch source digest: reject changed rows before a restart

Persistence and transaction failure boundaries

  • Spring Data JPA bulk update: the managed entity can still hold the old value
  • Spring Data JPA derived delete versus bulk delete: callbacks and memory cost
  • Spring Data JPA pessimistic lock: hold it only through the stock decision
  • Spring REQUIRES_NEW: budget the second database connection
  • Spring imperative transaction: a worker thread does not inherit it
  • Spring reactive transaction: subscription owns the context, not a thread

MongoDB and Elasticsearch boundaries

  • Spring Data MongoDB optimistic locking: save the version you read
  • Spring Data MongoDB tenant uniqueness: enforce it in an index
  • Spring Data MongoDB transaction: keep every write in one client session
  • Spring Data MongoDB bulk writes: fewer round trips, different lifecycle behavior
  • Spring Data MongoDB change stream: resume token and idempotent projection
  • Spring Data Elasticsearch write versus search: refresh is the visibility boundary
  • Spring Data Elasticsearch sequence conflict: do not overwrite a newer projection
  • Spring Data Elasticsearch mapping rollout: build a new index, then move the read alias

Cassandra and Neo4j data boundaries

  • Spring Data Cassandra partition keys: model the read before the row
  • Spring Data Cassandra TTL: expiry is a storage and query cost
  • Spring Data Cassandra paging state: continue the same bounded query
  • Spring Data Neo4j relationships: save only the graph you own
  • Spring Data Neo4j transaction: keep the command inside one managed unit
  • Spring Data Neo4j version conflicts: reject a stale graph update

Cassandra and Neo4j write and query contracts

  • Spring Data Cassandra conditional insert: reserve one key once
  • Spring Data Cassandra consistency: budget availability and staleness per operation
  • Spring Data Cassandra @Version: a conflict is not a merge
  • Spring Data Neo4j custom query: return one coherent root record
  • Spring Data Neo4j tenant lookup: constrain before traversing
  • Spring Data Neo4j relationship properties: preserve edge identity

JPA query and transaction contracts

  • Spring Data JPA entity graph for a bounded to-one read
  • Spring Data JPA Specifications with a mandatory tenant predicate
  • Spring Data JPA Page versus Slice: pay for totals only when needed
  • Spring Data JPA count query for a joined Page
  • Spring Data JPA saveAndFlush is a SQL boundary, not a commit
  • Spring read-only transaction: performance hint, not a write guard
  • Spring Data JPA auditing: record the actor at the write boundary
  • Spring Boot Open EntityManager in View: close the response-time query gap

Entity identity, collection loading and deadlines

  • Spring Data JPA assigned IDs: tell save when an entity is new
  • JPA detached merge: prevent partial requests from erasing stored fields
  • JPA entity equality: keep hash keys stable across persist and detach
  • JPA insert batching: bound both JDBC trips and persistence-context memory
  • JPA collection batch fetching: reduce N+1 without a giant join
  • JPA collection fetch and pagination: page IDs before loading children
  • Spring transaction timeout: put the deadline on the owning scope
  • JPA flush mode: know when pending writes become SQL

title: Security
summary: Authentication and browser boundaries
body:
Spring Security applies authentication, authorization and browser protections at request boundaries.

Learning roadmap

Read the contract, run the source-kit checks, and inspect a rejected input before extending the application. This subject covers Spring and Spring Boot together; Java language lessons remain in their own subject.

Prerequisites

Use Java object ownership, interfaces, exceptions and Maven builds before the framework-specific lessons.

Section lessons

  • Spring Security filter chain: authentication, CSRF and request order
  • Spring PasswordEncoder: salted verification rather than reversible storage
  • Spring method authorization: test the proxied service boundary
  • Spring Security JWT resource server: validate trust before checking scope
  • Spring method authorization: reject a cross-tenant read
  • Spring method security: reject a cross-tenant receipt mutation
  • Spring Security roles and authorities: check the actual granted string
  • Spring Security JWT tenant principal: map only a validated claim
  • Spring Security scope versus tenant ownership: two separate decisions
  • Spring JWT tenant claims: reject missing or malformed ownership before conversion
  • Spring JdbcTemplate tenant predicates: put ownership in the SQL query
  • Spring tenant headers: prove they cannot override a signed identity
  • Spring Security bearer POST and CSRF: define the credential boundary
  • Spring file uploads: discard the supplied filename before writing
  • Spring Security health probes: expose only the health path

Continue learning

Boot Foundations, Spring Core, Web APIs, Data & Transactions, Testing, Production, Exercises, Quizzes, Projects.

Request authorization and browser state

  • Spring Security request matchers: order rules and cover the fallback
  • Spring Security CSRF: protect cookie-authenticated writes

OAuth2 browser and service clients

  • Spring Security OAuth2 login: callback, identity and browser session
  • Spring OAuth2 client credentials: acquire and reuse a service token

GraphQL tenant boundaries

  • Spring GraphQL tenant reads: scope every resolver before returning a record

Spring Cloud boundary lessons

  • Spring Cloud Gateway tenant routing: authenticate at the edge and enforce again at the service

Spring AI boundary lessons

  • Spring AI prompt injection: treat retrieved text as data, not authority
  • Spring AI tools: authorize each requested action after model selection

Token and browser-session boundaries

  • Spring resource server JWT: validate both issuer and intended audience
  • Spring Security 401 versus 403: authentication and access are separate failures
  • Spring Security login session: rotate the identifier at authentication

Run an OAuth2 authorization server

  • Spring Authorization Server, OAuth2 client and resource server: three trust roles
  • Spring Authorization Server JDBC state: clients, grants and consent across restarts
  • Spring Authorization Server grants: PKCE for public clients, credentials for services

Shared sessions and nested query authorization

  • Spring Session Redis across replicas: shared login state has a Redis failure boundary
  • Spring Session cookie policy: SameSite, Secure and the reverse proxy
  • Spring Session principal index: invalidate one operator's sessions safely
  • Spring GraphQL batch loader tenant scope: never key a shared cache by row ID alone

Gateway and STOMP identity boundaries

  • Spring Cloud Gateway rate limits: derive the key from authenticated identity
  • Spring WebSocket STOMP identity: authenticate the handshake, authorize destinations

Outbound token ownership

  • Spring OAuth2 client tokens: bind the authorized client to the intended caller and host

Method-level authorization

  • Spring method security: authorization advice runs through the bean proxy
  • Spring @PostAuthorize: denial happens after the method has run

SAML identity and authority

  • Spring Security SAML relying party: align registration, ACS and metadata
  • Spring Security SAML validation: signatures, audience and clock window
  • Spring Security SAML attributes: map identity to local authority

SAML logout, sessions and certificate rollover

  • Spring Security SAML logout: local session versus single logout
  • Spring SAML session revocation: closing the browser is not deprovisioning
  • Spring SAML certificate rollover: overlap trust without accepting unknown keys

Security maintenance and request boundaries

  • Spring Resource Server JWT key rotation: overlap keys across token lifetime
  • Spring password hash upgrade after a verified login
  • Spring SecurityContext handoff to a bounded async executor
  • Spring Security CORS preflight: evaluate origin before authentication

Security chain and token boundaries

  • Spring Security multiple filter chains: match the whole request surface
  • Spring Security stateless APIs: remove session and saved-request assumptions
  • Spring JWT authority mapping: convert a trusted claim into one deliberate namespace
  • Spring JWT clock skew: bound tolerance without extending token trust blindly
  • Spring Security SPA CSRF: refresh the token after login and logout
  • Spring opaque-token introspection: budget the authorization-server dependency
  • Spring Security CSP rollout: enforce tested asset rules at the response edge
  • Spring method security ownership bean: authorize before the service changes state

summary: Choose the right test boundary
body:
Spring testing tools isolate object, container and HTTP contracts through selected fixtures.

Learning roadmap

Read the contract, run the source-kit checks, and inspect a rejected input before extending the application. This subject covers Spring and Spring Boot together; Java language lessons remain in their own subject.

Prerequisites

Use Java object ownership, interfaces, exceptions and Maven builds before the framework-specific lessons.

Section lessons

  • Spring MockMvc tests: HTTP behavior without claiming a real network test
  • Spring tests: separate business rules, wiring and transport
  • Spring ApplicationContextRunner: check conditional assembly in isolation
  • Spring MockMvc standalone tests: know which HTTP layers were assembled
  • Spring test failures: prove the layer that can reject the request
  • Test a Spring worker at admission, lease and replay boundaries
  • Test Spring JWT authorization through filters, service proxy and SQL
  • Spring command rollback test: inspect state after an injected failure
  • Spring MockMvc multipart tests: what the fixture proves
  • Spring relay failure trace: inspect persisted state at each cut point
  • Spring relay integration tests: prove the boundaries H2 cannot
  • Spring schema rollout tests: check old and new writers at every phase
  • Spring Boot migration tests: distinguish a test starter from a runtime rollout
  • Spring release tests: distinguish context checks from process and platform checks
  • Test Spring RestClient on a socket without claiming a remote service
  • Spring Boot config tests: what a child JVM proves and what deployment still owes
  • Spring Boot file-tree tests: prove binding without claiming secret delivery

Continue learning

Boot Foundations, Spring Core, Web APIs, Data & Transactions, Security, Production, Exercises, Quizzes, Projects.

Kafka verification layers

  • Spring Kafka testing layers: know what a direct listener test cannot prove

GraphQL test scope

  • Spring GraphQL service tests: stop short of claiming an HTTP endpoint

R2DBC dependency and test scope

  • Spring R2DBC fixture isolation: keep incompatible H2 versions out of one test classpath

Spring AI boundary lessons

  • Spring AI evaluations: separate model quality from enforced safety contracts

Modulith module and event boundaries

  • Spring Modulith verification: a compiling internal import still fails architecture checks
  • Spring Modulith module tests: distinguish structure verification from a sliced context

Batch fault handling

  • Spring Batch crash recovery: test the repository and input across two processes

Modulith event and module tests

  • Spring Modulith module slices: start inventory without dispatch
  • Spring Modulith PublishedEvents: assert an accepted fact and a rejected silence

Batch recovery and rejected-row review

  • Spring Batch restart test matrix: separate failure, process loss and changed input

Batch metadata and hard-stop recovery

  • Spring Batch restart tests: assert metadata rows, not repeated ID values

Testcontainers connection lifecycle

  • Spring Boot Testcontainers: service connections and cached-context lifecycle

Container schema and test isolation

  • Spring Boot Testcontainers and Flyway: let one owner prepare the test schema
  • Spring Testcontainers parallel tests: one database can leak another test's rows

Spring testing boundaries

  • Spring Data JPA test: flush and clear before trusting a read
  • Spring Data JPA test against the deployment database dialect
  • Spring Boot HTTP test: client rollback does not own server writes
  • Spring MockMvc security test: run the application filter chain
  • Spring TestContext cache: keep equivalent tests on one context shape
  • Spring @MockitoBean override: a mock can remove advice from the tested bean
  • Spring transactional event test: cross an actual commit boundary
  • Spring scheduled worker test: inject a clock and call the work once

Test slice and transaction boundaries

  • Spring @WebMvcTest: replace collaborators without claiming a full application
  • Spring MockMvc async dispatch: assert the final response after resumed handling
  • Spring @DynamicPropertySource: bind test resources without stale cached values
  • Spring @Sql fixtures: decide whether setup commits outside the test rollback
  • Spring @DirtiesContext: evict only a context a test truly changed
  • Spring RestClient mock server: assert outgoing request shape before socket tests
  • Spring WebTestClient target: distinguish mock binding from a running port
  • Spring transactional tests: preemptive timeouts can escape rollback

title: Production
summary: Capacity, cache and health boundaries
body:
Spring operational components expose health, task admission and cache behavior under explicit application policies.

Learning roadmap

Read the contract, run the source-kit checks, and inspect a rejected input before extending the application. This subject covers Spring and Spring Boot together; Java language lessons remain in their own subject.

Prerequisites

Use Java object ownership, interfaces, exceptions and Maven builds before the framework-specific lessons.

Section lessons

  • Spring Boot Actuator health: public liveness without public diagnostics
  • Spring task executors: capacity, rejection and lost context
  • Spring cache keys: separate tenants and test the loader count
  • Spring Boot metrics: bound tag values instead of tracking each receipt
  • Spring cache eviction: invalidate the same tenant key used by the read
  • Spring readiness: report an unavailable dependency without forcing liveness failure
  • Spring @Cacheable sync: collapse a local same-key cache miss
  • At-least-once delivery: where Spring outbox retries can duplicate work
  • Spring Boot readiness health group: withdraw traffic on a required dependency failure
  • Spring Boot liveness versus readiness: do not restart on every dependency outage
  • Spring outbox retries: due time, delay cap, and attempt accounting
  • Spring outbox retry budget: park a poison event for inspection
  • Spring outbox polling: cap work per tick and measure backlog age
  • Spring scheduled retries: leave failed work pending until its due time
  • Spring relay metrics: measure backlog without event-ID labels
  • Spring Boot graceful shutdown: finish accepted requests within a deadline
  • Spring worker shutdown: release admission before a lease expires
  • Spring readiness during termination: stop routing before stopping dependencies

Continue learning

Boot Foundations, Spring Core, Web APIs, Data & Transactions, Security, Testing, Exercises, Quizzes, Projects.

Batch jobs and trace context

  • Spring Batch chunk restart: know which receipts committed
  • Spring async trace context: follow work across executor threads

Kafka delivery boundaries

  • Spring Kafka manual acknowledgement: commit work before advancing the offset
  • Spring Kafka record keys: preserve per-SKU order without claiming global order
  • Spring Kafka producer future: observe broker send completion separately from command success
  • Spring Kafka listener failures: separate transient retries from poison records

Spring Cloud boundary lessons

  • Spring Cloud discovery: a service name locates an instance, not a trusted peer
  • Spring Cloud client retries: distinguish a safe read from an uncertain write
  • Spring Cloud Circuit Breaker: make fallback obey the original data contract

Spring AI boundary lessons

  • Spring AI ChatClient request budgets: bound latency, tokens and work per caller

Batch restart and recovery

  • Spring Batch job identity: a manifest ID defines restart versus a new run
  • Spring Batch skip and retry policy: distinguish bad input from temporary failure

Batch fault handling

  • Spring Batch skip limits: the next invalid receipt fails the step
  • Spring Batch retry exhaustion: a temporary error needs a finite stop
  • Spring Batch reconciliation: report accepted and rejected receipt IDs

Modulith event and module tests

  • Spring Modulith event registry recovery: separate publication, listener and broker states

Batch recovery and rejected-row review

  • Spring Batch restart across two JVMs after a recorded failed execution
  • Spring Batch orphaned STARTED execution: inspect before relaunch

Batch metadata and hard-stop recovery

  • Spring Boot 4 Batch JDBC starter: verify that job history is actually stored
  • Spring Batch killed worker: fence it, recover STARTED, then restart

Integration, streaming and scheduling boundaries

  • Spring Integration DirectChannel versus ExecutorChannel: where the transaction stops
  • Spring Integration queue: bound memory and choose a real message store
  • Spring Integration idempotent receiver: the metadata key is not the business commit
  • Spring Integration poller: include receive and handler in the failure boundary
  • Spring Cloud Stream consumer group: scale one logical reader without copying every event
  • Spring Cloud Stream Kafka DLQ: stop poison messages without losing the trail
  • Spring Cloud Stream producer failure: a sent message is not an accepted business command
  • Spring @Scheduled on three replicas: the callback runs three times

Rabbit delivery and trace handoffs

  • Spring AMQP prefetch: bound unacknowledged messages before raising concurrency
  • Spring AMQP poison messages: reject, requeue and dead-letter are different decisions
  • RabbitTemplate confirms and returns: broker acceptance is not consumer completion
  • Spring Boot tracing across RestClient: construct the client from Boot's builder
  • Spring Boot observation context across @Async and Reactor handoffs

Redis cache expiry and shared-writer behavior

  • Spring Redis cache TTL versus idle expiry: GETEX changes the read contract
  • Spring Redis cache key schema: tenant, prefix and rollout version
  • Spring Redis cache writer: compound operations and replica stampedes

Route changes and Redis operations

  • Spring Cloud Gateway route refresh: guard the actuator write boundary
  • Spring Data Redis Cluster: key slots change multi-key operations
  • Spring Redis cache outage: choose failure behavior per operation

Kubernetes configuration and discovery

  • Spring Cloud Kubernetes config import: make source precedence explicit
  • Spring Cloud Kubernetes reload: decide which changes need a restart
  • Spring Cloud Kubernetes discovery: choose API lookup or Service DNS

Kubernetes workload permissions and probes

  • Spring Cloud Kubernetes permissions: scope the service account to its reads
  • Spring Boot Kubernetes probes: separate startup, readiness and liveness
  • Spring Cloud Kubernetes watcher scope: filter before broadcasting refresh

Management and cache contracts

  • Spring Actuator management port: separate listener, explicit access rule
  • Spring Prometheus scrape endpoint: registry, exposure and label contract
  • Spring health details: status for probes, diagnostics for operators
  • Spring cache after commit: keep rolled-back writes out of readers
  • Spring null-result caching: decide whether a miss should survive
  • Spring Redis cache serialization: roll payload formats without mixed readers
  • Spring tracing and logs: preserve request identity across outbound calls
  • Spring Actuator loggers endpoint: temporary diagnosis with guarded write access

Logs, TLS rotation and startup evidence

  • Spring Boot structured logs: stable fields without customer data
  • Spring Boot SSL bundle rotation: replace certificate files with a verified handoff
  • Spring Boot startup timeline: measure context work before extending probes

Batch scope, checkpoint and scaling contracts

  • Spring Batch step scope: bind a reader to one execution
  • Spring Batch job scope: avoid a shared bean in partition workers
  • Spring Batch ExecutionContext keys: give each stream its own checkpoint
  • Spring Batch FlatFileItemReader: save state against an immutable source
  • Spring Batch partitioner: assign disjoint receipt ranges

title: Spring Core ownership quiz
summary: Twelve explained questions on spring core ownership.
body:
A Spring self-check tests spring core ownership using the source-kit contracts.

Review before answering

  • Spring ApplicationContext: construct and close an object graph
  • Spring constructor injection: required dependencies stay visible
  • Spring qualifiers: select a collaborator when types are ambiguous
  • Spring bean scopes: singleton identity is not thread safety
  • Spring ObjectProvider: deferred resolution without hiding ownership
  • Spring lifecycle cleanup: close container-owned resources
  • Spring application events: local delivery is not a durable queue
  • Spring AOP proxies: self-invocation bypasses proxy advice

Check your reasoning

Answer every question, then read the explanations. This browser self-check is not a credential or a server-side code judge.

Common Mistakes

Distinguish a checked local fixture from a production guarantee. Container ownership, database atomicity and request authorization require separate evidence.
subject: spring-quizzes

questions.prompt: What does a singleton scope guarantee for one bean definition in one context?
options: One instance for the entire network
questions.explanation: Instance reuse and thread safety are separate contracts.

questions.prompt: A prototype is injected once into a singleton. What does that field hold?
options: A new object for every method call
questions.explanation: Ordinary injection supplies one reference at construction or injection time.

questions.prompt: How does the kit request two fresh prototype buffers?
options: Two reads of one injected field
questions.explanation: Each prototype resolution creates an instance; a field read does not resolve it again.

questions.prompt: Two Exporter beans exist. A plain type lookup has no other selection rule. What is expected?
questions.explanation: The fixture expects NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException and uses a qualifier for intentional wiring.

questions.prompt: Why does the direct report unit test need no context?
options: Its collaborator is an ordinary constructor argument
questions.explanation: Required dependencies stay visible and can be supplied directly.

questions.prompt: What closes the fixture singleton ClosingChannel?
questions.explanation: The context delivers the destruction callback for this managed singleton.

questions.prompt: Does prototype scope provide the same managed destruction as singleton scope?
options: No; the caller owns cleanup after resolution
questions.explanation: Prototype initialization and destruction have different ownership rules.

questions.prompt: What does a local application event provide in this kit?
questions.explanation: The fixture is local and does not persist or replay work.

questions.prompt: The target outer method directly calls inner. How many proxy entries does the fixture advise?
questions.explanation: Only outer enters through the proxy reference; the target-to-target call does not.

questions.prompt: Does qualifier wiring validate a runtime document format?
questions.explanation: The qualifier chooses a bean during assembly, not a domain format policy.

questions.prompt: When should a test create a new full application context?
options: When the contract needs actual container assembly
questions.explanation: Select the smallest boundary that supplies the required evidence.

questions.prompt: Can a deferred provider conceal a missing required bean until runtime?
questions.explanation: Deferred resolution changes when lookup failure can occur, so mandatory dependencies need an intentional boundary.

questions.prompt: What does a fixed-delay poll interval measure?
options: Time after one callback finishes before the next begins
A hard deadline for each event
questions.explanation: The next invocation is scheduled after the prior callback completes. Transport time is separate.

questions.prompt: Three events are due and a tick has batch limit two. What should one checked tick leave?
questions.explanation: The fixture processes at most two candidates per call; a second call handles the remaining row.

questions.prompt: Why does the claim UPDATE repeat due-time and lease predicates after the SELECT?
options: Another worker may change the row between selection and claim
questions.explanation: The conditional mutation decides ownership against current row state.

questions.prompt: A fake transport fails once in the scheduled test. What happens next?
options: The same event ID remains pending until its due time
The row is marked delivered immediately
A new event ID is generated
questions.explanation: The poller increments its failure count, clears the claim and stores a future due time.

questions.prompt: What does cancelling the scheduled future prove?
options: Future callbacks from that local schedule stop
An in-flight broker publish is rolled back
questions.explanation: Cancellation controls this scheduler registration; external work and restart recovery need separate checks.

questions.prompt: Two H2 workers select the same pending event. Which operation decides the current claim owner?
questions.explanation: Only the guarded mutation checks current state and returns one changed row to the winner.

questions.prompt: Worker A’s lease expires and B reclaims the event. May A renew it afterward?
options: Yes, if it proposes a later deadline
Yes, if it still has the event payload
questions.explanation: Renewal requires the current token and an unexpired current lease.

body:

Review before answering

  • Spring MVC ProblemDetail: stable errors without leaking internals
  • Spring API pagination: bounded requests and immutable snapshots
  • Spring MVC CORS: a browser-origin policy is not authentication
  • Spring Security filter chain: authentication, CSRF and request order
  • Spring PasswordEncoder: salted verification rather than reversible storage
  • Spring MockMvc tests: HTTP behavior without claiming a real network test
  • Spring Security JWT tenant principal: map only a validated claim
  • Spring Security scope versus tenant ownership: two separate decisions
  • Spring JWT tenant claims: reject missing or malformed ownership before conversion
  • Spring JdbcTemplate tenant predicates: put ownership in the SQL query
  • Test Spring JWT authorization through filters, service proxy and SQL
  • Spring MVC multipart receipt import: validate before storing
  • Spring multipart size limits: enforce parser and application budgets
  • Spring file uploads: discard the supplied filename before writing
  • Spring MockMvc multipart tests: what the fixture proves
  • Spring Boot readiness health group: withdraw traffic on a required dependency failure
  • Spring Security health probes: expose only the health path

Check your reasoning

Answer every question, then read the explanations. This browser self-check is not a credential or a server-side code judge.

Common Mistakes

Distinguish a checked local fixture from a production guarantee. Container ownership, database atomicity and request authorization require separate evidence.
subject: spring-quizzes

questions.prompt: What does a positive amount constraint prove?
options: The input value meets that constraint
questions.explanation: Validation does not establish authorization or settlement.

questions.prompt: Which response does the kit promise for a created valid receipt?
questions.explanation: The controller test checks creation status and the response amount.

questions.prompt: Why repeat an amount invariant inside the store?
options: Non-HTTP callers can bypass controller validation
questions.explanation: Domain invariants belong to the business boundary as well as the transport boundary.

questions.prompt: What does ProblemDetail avoid requiring a client to parse?
questions.explanation: A structured error keeps public behavior separate from internal diagnostics.

questions.prompt: Does a standalone MockMvc setup automatically prove the real security chain?
options: No; include security integration for that claim
Only when the controller is final
questions.explanation: Supplied controllers and validators are a narrower boundary than the full filter chain.

questions.prompt: Is CORS user authentication?
questions.explanation: A browser origin policy does not identify or authorize a user.

questions.prompt: A Basic header is present but CSRF validation rejects before authentication. Must the result be 403?
options: No; filter order can lead to a 401 challenge
questions.explanation: The kit checks pre-authentication rejection separately from established-user rejection.

questions.prompt: What happens to a protected POST with an established test user but no CSRF token?
questions.explanation: The filter-chain test confirms forbidden mutation for that established-user request.

questions.prompt: Two encodings of the same password differ. Is verification necessarily broken?
options: Only if the password is long
questions.explanation: Use matches with the stored encoding rather than comparing a freshly encoded string.

questions.prompt: Does a page of twenty rows imply O(20) work in this in-memory store?
options: No; it copies the whole collection first
questions.explanation: Response size and the cost of producing the response are different dimensions.

questions.prompt: What does the immutable returned page prevent?
options: All future updates to the store
questions.explanation: Container immutability does not freeze unrelated service state or arbitrary referenced elements.

questions.prompt: May the source-kit local-reader account be treated as production identity storage?
options: Yes if the name is changed
Yes if the port is random
questions.explanation: It is a reproducible fixture; deployment needs real credential and account ownership.

questions.prompt: A signed receipt.read token names tenant-east. What should /contract/tenant/tenant-west return in the checked fixture?
questions.explanation: The token is trusted and has the scope, but the managed service rejects a different tenant argument.

questions.prompt: A trusted tenant-east token has receipt.write but calls a receipt.read endpoint. Which layer denies it?
questions.explanation: The filter chain requires SCOPE_receipt.read before invoking the service.

questions.prompt: A trusted token has receipt.read but omits tenant_id. What does the local decoder do?
questions.explanation: The required tenant claim validator rejects the token before principal conversion.

questions.prompt: Can X-Tenant: tenant-west override a validated tenant-east JWT in the source-kit context?
options: No, the header is ignored for ownership
questions.explanation: The test sends a spoofed header in both accepted and denied requests; the signed claim remains the identity source.

questions.prompt: R-41 exists for east and west. What must the repository lookup bind?
options: Receipt ID and trusted tenant ID
questions.explanation: The scoped H2 query uses both values; filtering after an unscoped read is too late.

questions.prompt: What does the local JWT tenant test leave unproved?
options: Remote issuer rotation and deployed proxy behavior
questions.explanation: The test uses temporary keys, a local web context and H2; remote identity and deployment need separate checks.

questions.prompt: A multipart part says its original filename is ../../outside.csv. Which path does the checked controller write?
options: A generated file inside the temporary storage root
The parent directory named by the client
No file because every slash is rejected
questions.explanation: The accepted request ignores the supplied filename for storage and verifies the generated path.

questions.prompt: A part claims text/csv but contains HTML. What does the local upload fixture return?
questions.explanation: The checked header gate rejects the bytes before creating a file; the MIME declaration is caller controlled.

questions.prompt: What does standalone MockMvc fail to prove for an oversized multipart request?
options: That rejected requests leave the JUnit directory empty
questions.explanation: MockMultipartFile already holds the bytes and does not run the deployed parser or proxy.

questions.prompt: The test-only importStore indicator changes from UP to DOWN. Which response pair is checked?
questions.explanation: Only the readiness group includes the indicator; the process liveness signal stays healthy.

questions.prompt: Nested health paths are public in the source kit. What happens to anonymous GET /api/receipts?
questions.explanation: The filter matcher permits only the health path and nested health groups before requiring authentication elsewhere.

questions.prompt: What remains outside the checked multipart fixture?
options: A deployed servlet parser, durable storage and full CSV row validation
questions.explanation: The controller is standalone; no production upload route or parser pipeline has been deployed.

title: Spring data and production contract quiz
summary: Twenty-five explained questions on Spring data, delivery and tenant command boundaries.
body:
A Spring self-check tests spring data and production contract using the source-kit contracts.

Review before answering

  • Spring JdbcTemplate: bound values and visible database constraints
  • Spring TransactionTemplate: roll back a failed multi-row change
  • Spring transactional methods: call paths and rollback assumptions
  • Spring task executors: capacity, rejection and lost context
  • Spring cache keys: separate tenants and test the loader count
  • Spring Boot Actuator health: public liveness without public diagnostics
  • Spring Boot receipt API project: build, test and inspect the limits
  • Spring task executors: reject work when every slot is occupied
  • Spring outbox claims: allow recovery after a worker lease expires
  • Outbox acknowledgements: require the current lease token
  • Spring consumer deduplication: commit the event ID with the mutation
  • At-least-once delivery: where Spring outbox retries can duplicate work
  • Spring tenant command transaction: keep state, event and replay record together
  • Spring POST idempotency keys: bind replay to tenant and command
  • Spring JDBC versioned tenant update: inspect the affected row count
  • Spring receipt outbox command: record intent without claiming delivery
  • Spring command rollback test: inspect state after an injected failure
  • Spring exercise: trace tenant command replay, denial and rollback

Check your reasoning

Answer every question, then read the explanations. This browser self-check is not a credential or a server-side code judge.

Common Mistakes

Distinguish a checked local fixture from a production guarantee. Container ownership, database atomicity and request authorization require separate evidence.
subject: spring-quizzes

questions.prompt: What does placeholder binding protect in the ledger insert?
questions.explanation: SQL structure stays fixed; structural choices need a separate allowlist.

questions.prompt: A transaction inserts one valid row then violates a constraint. What does the kit check afterward?
questions.explanation: Persisted state after failure is the evidence for rollback.

questions.prompt: A transaction callback marks rollback-only and returns normally. Must it commit?
questions.explanation: The transaction state explicitly requests rollback despite normal callback return.

questions.prompt: Can JDBC rollback retract an HTTP operation already accepted by another server?
options: Yes if called in a callback
questions.explanation: Local database atomicity cannot reverse an independent external side effect.

questions.prompt: Does H2 prove every production database lock and isolation behavior?
questions.explanation: The local fixture needs separate target-database evidence before production isolation claims.

questions.prompt: A bounded executor rejects its third task. Should the service silently claim success?
questions.explanation: Rejected admission needs a visible application outcome.

questions.prompt: Does a queue capacity of one bound retained payload bytes to one byte?
questions.explanation: A queued closure can retain a large payload; task count and bytes are separate bounds.

questions.prompt: What is missing from a cache key containing only receiptId in a multi-tenant lookup?
questions.explanation: The fixture includes tenant and receipt identifier so results do not cross owners.

questions.prompt: The kit uses ConcurrentMapCacheManager. Does that supply distributed invalidation?
questions.explanation: This context-local cache has no distributed consistency or eviction policy.

questions.prompt: Why check the loader call count in the cache test?
options: Identical output alone does not prove cache hits
questions.explanation: The counter confirms which requests actually reached the target loader.

questions.prompt: Does public health access imply all management endpoints are public?
options: No; endpoint exposure and authorization are explicit
questions.explanation: The fixture allows anonymous health and protects other paths.

questions.prompt: Where does the receipt API actually store its receipts?
questions.explanation: The project makes the persistence limit explicit; the JDBC fixture is not wired as its repository.

questions.prompt: One receipt task runs and one waits in a one-thread, one-slot executor. What should the default policy do with a third submission?
questions.explanation: The bounded executor fixture observes TaskRejectedException. Neither running nor queued work is durable.

questions.prompt: Worker-A holds an outbox lease until logical time 200. Can worker-B claim the row at time 150?
options: Yes, if it uses a different token
No, the prior lease is still valid
Yes, if the event is old
questions.explanation: The conditional update refuses a second claim before expiry.

questions.prompt: After worker-B reclaims an expired row, what should worker-A's acknowledgement update?
options: Every row for the same receipt
questions.explanation: A current claim token in the update predicate fences a stale owner from changing the row.

questions.prompt: Why record an event ID and apply the stock mutation in one transaction?
options: To make broker delivery exactly once
To make a failed mutation roll back its dedup record
To avoid a database uniqueness constraint
questions.explanation: The local fixture checks both repeat suppression and rollback of an event ID after a failed stock change.

questions.prompt: A relay sends E-41 and stops before it can persist acknowledgement. What can a retry do?
questions.explanation: The send and database acknowledgement have a failure window; the destination needs its own duplicate rule.

questions.prompt: What does the local outbox lease test establish about two deployed replicas?
options: Their concurrent claims are safe under load
Only sequential H2 lease and token outcomes
questions.explanation: The checked fixture uses deterministic times and sequential statements; deployment concurrency still needs a target-database test.

questions.prompt: A tenant-east write commits a receipt, an outbox row and a replay row. What makes those three writes atomic in the local fixture?
options: A single H2 transaction using one DataSource
questions.explanation: TransactionTemplate encloses all three JDBC writes on one DataSource. The token controls identity, not database commit.

questions.prompt: A POST retry uses the same tenant, key, receipt, state and expected version. What should happen?
options: Return the stored version without a second event
Reject it as a stale write
questions.explanation: The replay row is checked before the versioned update, so the accepted response can be returned again.

questions.prompt: The same tenant and key are reused for another receipt ID. How does the fixture respond?
questions.explanation: The command fingerprint includes the receipt ID, so the reused key cannot identify a different command.

questions.prompt: A write expects version 3 while the stored row is version 1. What remains after the request?
options: The state changes and no event is stored
No state change, event or replay row
An event is stored for later repair
questions.explanation: The parameterized update affects zero rows, raises a conflict and exits the transaction before inserts.

questions.prompt: The service throws after inserting the outbox row but before inserting its replay row. Which result is checked?
options: The receipt commits while the replay row disappears
questions.explanation: The test inspects the receipt, outbox and replay tables after the injected failure.

questions.prompt: Does a committed outbox row mean an external consumer received the event?
options: Yes, the transaction spans the broker
No, delivery and acknowledgement are separate work
Only when the JWT has receipt.write
questions.explanation: The local command fixture records intent in H2; it does not run a relay, broker or consumer.

questions.prompt: Why is an accepted east write with X-Tenant: tenant-west still an east write?
options: The trusted JWT claim and service rule supply tenant ownership
The header is signed by the database
The URL path always overrides the token
questions.explanation: The header is request data. The method rule compares the requested tenant with the validated token principal.

questions.prompt: A producer inserts a shipment request and outbox row, then throws an unchecked exception in the same transaction. What should remain?
questions.explanation: The checked TransactionTemplate callback rolls both inserts back; delivery has not begun.

questions.prompt: A consumer commits stock and its applied-event marker, but the relay loses its acknowledgement. What protects the retry?
options: The same event ID and unique applied-event key
questions.explanation: The retry may reach the consumer again. Its unique key rejects a second mutation for the same event.

questions.prompt: Worker A has a lease until logical time 120. At 120 worker B reclaims the event. Can A acknowledge at 121?
options: No, its claim token is stale
Yes, if the event ID matches
Yes, if its publish was fast
questions.explanation: The acknowledgement checks both the current token and an unexpired lease.

questions.prompt: An event has failed three times under a three-failure budget. What does the local claim query do?
options: It immediately gives the row a fourth claim
questions.explanation: The third failure parks the row in DEAD; only PENDING rows are claimable.

questions.prompt: What does OutboxRelayFlowTest prove about delivery?
options: Sequential H2 state transitions and local transaction results
Concurrent claims on the production database
questions.explanation: The fixture is in-process with a logical clock; broker and target-database checks remain separate.

title: Spring JPA entity lifecycle: managed changes and detached objects
summary: A JPA persistence context tracks managed entity identity and changes; an ordinary detached object no longer writes its field changes to the database.
body:
A JPA persistence context tracks managed entity identity and changes; an ordinary detached object no longer writes its field changes to the database.

The downloadable Spring source kit pins Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.0.8 with its managed dependencies. Run mvn test to check the named fixture.

Observe the ownership transition

The stock fixture creates three accounts, then changes the first account through an EntityManager bound to a Spring JpaTransactionManager transaction. A fresh manager reads 80 after commit. The test does not call a repository save method because the object is already managed within that transaction.

The second test closes the manager before changing an account to seven. A fresh read still returns 100. Java object mutation happened, but database mutation did not. Keep that distinction visible when returning entities from a service; a caller holding an object is not evidence that its edits are being tracked.

Flush is not commit

The source kit assembles LocalContainerEntityManagerFactoryBean explicitly, scans only the isolated contract package and uses create-drop against a unique in-memory H2 database. This setup exists to test mapping behavior. Never turn that schema setting into a production migration strategy.

A flush can send changes to the database before commit, while the transaction can still fail or roll back. Query timing and transaction scope therefore matter even when code contains no explicit update call. Transaction boundaries and JDBC commit behavior are prerequisites for reasoning about these effects.

Checked source

var transactions = new TransactionTemplate(new JpaTransactionManager(kit.factory));
transactions.executeWithoutResult(status -> {
    EntityManager manager = EntityManagerFactoryUtils.getTransactionalEntityManager(kit.factory);
    manager.find(JpaContracts.StockAccount.class, 1L).available = 80;
});

  • Do not treat flush as successful commit.

title: Spring JPA fetch plans: measure N+1 queries before changing mappings
summary: A fetch plan determines which related entity state a query loads, and lazy relationship traversal can issue extra statements after the root query.
body:
A fetch plan determines which related entity state a query loads, and lazy relationship traversal can issue extra statements after the root query.

The downloadable Spring source kit pins Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.0.8 with its managed dependencies. Run mvn test to check the named fixture.

Count statements in a fresh context

The fixture stores three stock lines, each linked to a distinct account. One query loads the lines, then reading each account’s available count produces three extra statements. The assertion checks four prepared statements after clearing Hibernate statistics. This makes the cost visible instead of inferring it from a method name.

Read account state through the getter: direct public-field access on a lazy proxy does not trigger its loading method. The test checks that distinction before traversal. A second test uses a new context and a join fetch for the single-valued account association. The same total, 300, now requires one statement. The fresh context matters: reusing already-loaded account objects could hide the extra queries and make an inefficient traversal appear cheap.

Fetch only what the operation needs

Switching every relationship to eager loading can move extra work to requests that never need it. Choose a query for the actual response contract, or return a projection that contains just the required fields. Query count is one measure; row width, transferred bytes and execution plans still matter.

This example fetches a many-to-one association. Fetching a collection can multiply result rows, and applying page limits to such a join needs separate reasoning. Offset bounds do not prove collection fetch pagination is correct. The lesson does not claim that its single statement is the best plan for every database.

Checked source

var lines = manager.createQuery(
    "select line from StockLine line join fetch line.account order by line.id",
    JpaContracts.StockLine.class).getResultList();
int total = 0;
for (var line : lines) total += line.account.getAvailable();
assertEquals(300, total);
assertEquals(1, kit.statistics().getPrepareStatementCount());

Test the boundary

Costs and boundaries

The checked traversal reads three lines and three accounts. The lazy path has 1+n statements for n distinct unloaded accounts in this mapping; the fetch path has one statement but still transfers and retains the required rows. Both counts are isolated local measurements, not latency benchmarks.

Common Mistakes

  • Clear provider statistics and use a fresh context before comparing query counts.
  • Do not make every relationship eager to fix one request.
  • Do not apply collection-fetch pagination rules to a single-valued join blindly.

title: Spring JPA optimistic locking: reject a stale stock update
summary: A versioned JPA entity detects an update based on an older revision so one writer cannot silently overwrite a newer committed revision.
body:
A versioned JPA entity detects an update based on an older revision so one writer cannot silently overwrite a newer committed revision.

The downloadable Spring source kit pins Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.0.8 with its managed dependencies. Run mvn test to check the named fixture.

Construct two independent views

Two EntityManagers load the same stock account before either changes it. The first writer commits 90 available units. The second still holds the earlier revision and tries to write 70. The test expects OptimisticLockException at flush, then rolls back the failed transaction.

The entity has one Long version field marked Version. Application code changes available, not the version. This fixture performs an ordered two-view experiment; it reproduces a stale write without claiming to simulate every possible concurrency schedule or database isolation level.

A retry must repeat the decision

Catching the exception and resubmitting the old desired value can still discard the business intent behind a competing update. Reload current stock and recompute the reservation under the intended contract, with a bounded retry policy. A failed transaction’s persistence context should not be reused as though it were healthy.

Versioning one account does not protect an invariant spanning several unversioned rows. It also does not stop duplicate external side effects from a retry. Multi-object invariants and Transaction scope need explicit treatment before applying this to a real inventory service.

Checked source

try (var first = kit.factory.createEntityManager();
     var second = kit.factory.createEntityManager()) {
    var current = first.find(JpaContracts.StockAccount.class, 1L);
    var stale = second.find(JpaContracts.StockAccount.class, 1L);
    first.getTransaction().begin();
    current.available = 90;
    first.getTransaction().commit();
    second.getTransaction().begin();
    stale.available = 70;
    assertThrows(OptimisticLockException.class, second::flush);
    second.getTransaction().rollback();
}

Costs and boundaries

A version check adds revision data to the update predicate and failure handling to the application. Contention can increase retries and database work. The local test proves rejection for one stale account update; it does not prove multi-row serializability or quantify throughput.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not edit the version manually.
  • Roll back after a failed flush.
  • Do not retry a stale decision without re-reading the state it depends on.

title: Spring transaction propagation: joined rollback and independent commit
summary: Transaction propagation determines whether a call joins an existing transaction or runs with another transaction boundary.
body:
Transaction propagation determines whether a call joins an existing transaction or runs with another transaction boundary.

The downloadable Spring source kit pins Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.0.8 with its managed dependencies. Run mvn test to check the named fixture.

Joined work shares rollback fate

TransactionContracts starts a REQUIRED outer transaction and inserts a pending journal row. An inner REQUIRED template marks its status rollback-only. The outer callback returns normally, but its attempted commit raises UnexpectedRollbackException and the table stays empty. Catching an inner application exception would not necessarily make the transaction committable.

The fixture uses templates so the propagation boundary is visible without proxy routing. An annotation-based service needs the call to cross the appropriate proxy; self-invocation can bypass the intended interception. Read Transaction proxies before translating this template into service annotations.

Independent work has an independent consequence

The second path inserts a pending row in the outer transaction, suspends it for REQUIRES_NEW, and commits a different audit row. The outer then rolls back. Only the audit row remains. That behavior is appropriate only if an audit entry is intended to survive a failed import.

An independent transaction can need another connection while the outer one remains held. The fixture uses separate H2 connections and unrelated primary keys. A bounded pool or shared locked row can change failure behavior; nesting REQUIRES_NEW under load needs a pool-capacity and lock analysis. Connection-pool boundaries provide that context.

Checked source

package in.aitrove.contracts;
import java.util.UUID;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate;
import org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.*;
import org.springframework.transaction.*;
import org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate;
public class TransactionContracts {
    public final JdbcTemplate jdbc;
    public final PlatformTransactionManager manager;
    public TransactionContracts() {
        var data=new DriverManagerDataSource("jdbc:h2:mem:propagation_"+UUID.randomUUID()+";DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1","sa","");
        jdbc=new JdbcTemplate(data); manager=new DataSourceTransactionManager(data);
        jdbc.execute("create table journal(id int primary key, message varchar(30))");
    }
    public TransactionTemplate transaction(int propagation) {
        var tx=new TransactionTemplate(manager);tx.setPropagationBehavior(propagation);return tx;
    }
    public void independentAuditSurvivesRollback() {
        transaction(TransactionDefinition.PROPAGATION_REQUIRED).executeWithoutResult(outer -> {
            jdbc.update("insert into journal values(1,'pending')");
            transaction(TransactionDefinition.PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW).executeWithoutResult(inner ->
                jdbc.update("insert into journal values(2,'audit')"));
            outer.setRollbackOnly();
        });
    }
    public void joinedRollbackRejectsCommit() {
        transaction(TransactionDefinition.PROPAGATION_REQUIRED).executeWithoutResult(outer -> {
            jdbc.update("insert into journal values(3,'pending')");
            transaction(TransactionDefinition.PROPAGATION_REQUIRED).executeWithoutResult(inner -> inner.setRollbackOnly());
        });
    }
    public int count() { return jdbc.queryForObject("select count(*) from journal",Integer.class); }
}

Test the boundary

Costs and boundaries

The test verifies two propagation paths, not every database schedule. Suspending a transaction retains its resources until resumed. An inner independent transaction adds connection demand and cannot be assumed to avoid deadlocks merely because it has a separate name.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not assume an outer commit succeeds after joined work marked rollback-only.
  • Choose intentionally whether an audit must survive rollback.
  • Budget extra connections for independent nested transactions.

title: Spring transaction events: run a listener after commit without claiming durability
summary: A TransactionalEventListener can defer an event callback until a selected transaction phase, such as AFTER_COMMIT.
body:
A TransactionalEventListener can defer an event callback until a selected transaction phase, such as AFTER_COMMIT.

The downloadable Spring source kit pins Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.0.8 with its managed dependencies. Run mvn test to check the named fixture.

Publish in the transaction you mean

The event fixture publishes an imported receipt three ways: outside a transaction, inside a rolled-back transaction, and inside a committed transaction. With default fallback behavior, only the committed event reaches the AFTER_COMMIT list. The test checks the final list contains the third receipt alone.

The list is ordinary process-local state and the listener runs in the test thread. This makes the phase contract inspectable. It does not provide a queue, durable log, separate worker or cross-process delivery mechanism. Ordinary application events and transaction-bound listeners have different timing rules.

A completed commit cannot be undone by the listener

When the listener starts after commit, the original database transaction has already succeeded. A listener failure must be handled as a post-commit failure; presenting it as though the original insert rolled back would lie to the caller. A fresh database write from this phase needs its own explicit transaction design.

A process can stop after committing a row and before delivering an in-memory callback. An outbox design addresses that gap by writing delivery intent with the business transaction and processing it separately. This lesson identifies the gap; it does not ship a durable outbox or an exactly-once consumer.

Checked source

package in.aitrove.contracts;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import org.springframework.transaction.event.*;
public class CommitEvents {
    public record ImportedReceipt(int id) {}
    public final List<Integer> committed=new ArrayList<>();
    @TransactionalEventListener(phase=TransactionPhase.AFTER_COMMIT)
    public void committed(ImportedReceipt event) { committed.add(event.id()); }
}

Test the boundary

FrameworkBoundaryTest.afterCommitDoesNotRunOnRollbackOrWithoutTransaction checks this contract in the source kit. Excerpts belong to the named classes; use the downloadable files for imports, configuration and assertions.

Costs and boundaries

The callback list grows with observed events and is unbounded in this teaching fixture. A production listener needs retention, concurrency and failure policies. AFTER_COMMIT describes timing; it supplies neither durable storage nor a latency limit.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not treat an in-memory callback as durable message delivery.
  • Do not assume a listener failure can roll back an already committed transaction.
  • Do not rely on default delivery outside a transaction.

title: Spring method authorization: test the proxied service boundary
summary: Method authorization intercepts a service invocation and evaluates an access rule before the protected method executes.
body:
Method authorization intercepts a service invocation and evaluates an access rule before the protected method executes.

The downloadable Spring source kit pins Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.0.8 with its managed dependencies. Run mvn test to check the named fixture.

Protect the service operation

AuthorizedReceiptRead requires receipt:read through PreAuthorize. The configuration explicitly enables method security, then the test obtains the bean from the context. A caller with that authority receives receipt:7; an authenticated caller without it receives AccessDeniedException. Authentication and authorization are separate questions.

The test installs a SecurityContext only for its local invocation and clears it in finally. It does not verify a login flow, tokens, sessions or a persistent identity store. HTTP filter rules remain necessary because they govern the request boundary that calls this service.

An annotation does not protect every Java object

The test also constructs AuthorizedReceiptRead directly. That object returns the receipt because it has no method-security proxy. This is intentional evidence of the boundary: an annotation is metadata, while interception supplies the enforcement path. Do not expose an unproxied copy of the service as a bypass.

The authority rule permits reading receipts in general. It does not prove ownership of receipt seven or enforce tenant membership. Add resource-specific authorization using trusted identity and repository state when the domain requires it. A route parameter supplied by the caller is not evidence of permission.

Checked source

package in.aitrove.contracts;
import org.springframework.security.access.prepost.PreAuthorize;
public class AuthorizedReceiptRead {
    @PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('receipt:read')")
    public String receipt(long id) { return "receipt:"+id; }
}

  • Enable method security and test the bean obtained from the context.
  • Do not assume direct construction enforces the annotation.
  • Do not confuse a general authority with ownership of a particular record.

title: Spring Boot metrics: bound tag values instead of tracking each receipt
summary: A Micrometer meter identity includes its name and tags, so a new tag value can create another series rather than another sample in the same series.
body:
A Micrometer meter identity includes its name and tags, so a new tag value can create another series rather than another sample in the same series.

The downloadable Spring source kit pins Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.0.8 with its managed dependencies. Run mvn test to check the named fixture.

Model a finite outcome set

The import metric has two outcomes: ACCEPTED and REJECTED. BoundedImportMetrics receives that enum rather than arbitrary strings. Recording one hundred accepted records and one rejected record creates exactly two local meters, with the accepted counter at one hundred.

The test uses SimpleMeterRegistry so the identity count is visible without a remote backend. Adding receipt IDs, email addresses or request paths containing identifiers would change both retained state and exported series count. Such values also risk placing sensitive data in telemetry.

Local meter count is not backend cost

A remote monitoring system may retain older time series after an application stops exporting them. Multiplying finite tag dimensions can still create many combinations: tenant, region and outcome counts must be budgeted together. A bounded enum only constrains the dimension it owns.

Use logs or traces with an explicit retention and privacy policy when investigating a specific record. Do not solve cardinality by silently dropping a business metric without checking what operations needs to answer. Health probes tell a different story from import counters.

package in.aitrove.contracts;
import io.micrometer.core.instrument.MeterRegistry;
public class BoundedImportMetrics {
    public enum Outcome { ACCEPTED, REJECTED }
    private final MeterRegistry registry;
    public BoundedImportMetrics(MeterRegistry registry) { this.registry=registry; }
    public void record(Outcome outcome) {
        registry.counter("receipt.import.records", "outcome",outcome.name()).increment();
    }
}

title: Spring reactive foundations: request values and cancel a subscription
summary: Reactive demand is a subscriber’s request for a bounded number of values from a publisher, while cancellation ends that subscription’s interest in further signals.
body:
Reactive demand is a subscriber’s request for a bounded number of values from a publisher, while cancellation ends that subscription’s interest in further signals.

The downloadable Spring source kit pins Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.0.8 with its managed dependencies. Run mvn test to check the named fixture.

Begin with zero demand

The Reactor fixture supplies five integer receipt markers. StepVerifier subscribes with an initial request of zero, asks for two values, expects one and two, then cancels. A separate assertion checks the cancellation hook. Another test requests all five and observes completion.

This is a Reactor Core sequence, not a WebFlux HTTP endpoint. Keeping that distinction explicit avoids claiming a transport, request-body buffer limit or network backpressure policy from a small in-memory publisher test. The sequence runs without a scheduler switch or blocking database call.

Demand is not a universal resource limit

An operator can prefetch or buffer upstream work, so a downstream request of two does not imply every upstream resource holds exactly two items. Cancellation also cannot undo a payment or database commit that already happened. Design cleanup and side-effect boundaries independently.

A blocking repository call inside a reactive callback still blocks its executing thread. Replacing an MVC return type with a publisher does not convert that repository into nonblocking I/O. Worker capacity and Cancellation rules remain relevant before moving this model into an HTTP service.

package in.aitrove.contracts;
import reactor.core.publisher.Flux;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean;
public class ReactiveReceiptDemand {
    public static Flux<Integer> records(AtomicBoolean cancelled) {
        return Flux.range(1,5).doOnCancel(() -> cancelled.set(true));
    }
}

Costs and boundaries

Common Mistakes

  • Do not treat demand as a rollback mechanism.
  • Do not hide blocking I/O behind a publisher return type.
  • Test cancellation cleanup separately from normal completion.

title: Spring Data JPA repositories: derive a query from mapped properties
summary: A Spring Data JPA repository creates a proxy that implements persistence operations and query methods against mapped entity properties.
body:
A Spring Data JPA repository creates a proxy that implements persistence operations and query methods against mapped entity properties.

The downloadable Spring source kit pins Java 21 and Spring Boot 4.0.8 with its managed dependencies. Run mvn test to check the named fixture.

Make the predicate readable

StockRepository declares findByAvailableGreaterThanOrderByIdAsc. The suffix describes a strict greater-than predicate and an ascending identifier order; it refers to the Java entity property, not an arbitrary database column alias. The fixture changes account two to thirty available units, then a threshold of fifty returns accounts one and three. A threshold of one hundred returns no rows.

The repository is created with JpaRepositoryFactory and a shared EntityManager so its boundary is visible in a small fixture. The shared manager resolves the transaction-bound persistence context; it is not one manually shared mutable EntityManager used by multiple request threads. A Boot application normally registers repositories through its configured scanning path.

Writes need a transaction policy

The stock change executes within TransactionTemplate and becomes a dirty-checking update when the transaction commits. Fetching an entity and changing it after its context has closed does not imply the same outcome. Entity lifecycle explains managed and detached state.

A convenient method name does not prove an acceptable query plan. The result list in this fixture is small; a production stock search needs a limit, an index analysis and an explicit access policy. If the predicate grows into a long business sentence, a reviewed explicit query can be easier to maintain than an increasingly complicated derived name.
